sections.title: Multi-step Ratio Problems
sections.content: Calculate ratios over multiple steps. Example: A:B:C = 2:3:4, C=12 → A=2*12/4=6, B=3*12/4=9.

sections.title: Inverse Ratio
sections.content: For work, time, speed, use inverse proportionality. Example: A completes in 10 days, B in 20 → A:B=20:10=2:1.

sections.title: Cyclical/Chain Ratios
sections.content: Combine multiple ratios in a chain. Example: A:B=3:4, B:C=5:6 → A:C=3×5:4×6=15:24.

sections.title: Indirect/Hidden Ratios
sections.content: Ratios with hidden variables. Example: Total investment ₹5000, A+B=3:2, B+C=4:5 → find A, B, C.

sections.title: Mixture + Percentage Link
sections.content: Adjust ratios when percentage change occurs. Example: Milk:Water=3:2, total ₹500, remove 10% water → new ratio=3:1.8≈5:3.

sections.title: Advanced Age Problems
sections.content: Use ratios over present and future ages. Example: Father:Son=7:3, 5 years later=9:4 → find current ages.

sections.title: Partnership with Variable Time
sections.content: Profit = Investment × Time. Example: A ₹2000 6 months, B ₹3000 8 months → A:B profit=12:24=1:2.

sections.title: Profit/Loss Multi-stage
sections.content: Multiple investors with different times. Example: A ₹1000 3 months, B ₹2000 6 months, C ₹1500 4 months, total profit=₹1000 → A=₹143, B=₹400, C=₹450.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
• Reverse steps incorrectly
• Forget inverse ratio
• Multiply incorrectly in chain ratios
• Skip hidden variables

sections.title: Quick Tips
sections.content:
• Simplify ratios at each step
• Cross-multiply carefully
• Work×Time=Inverse ratio, Investment×Time=Profit
• Use mini calculations for multi-step problems
